newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firm on refinery snags.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firm on refinery snags.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed firmer on Friday, buoyed by refinery problems in northwest Europe and a reversal of losses on crude futures, traders said.

August gas oil ended $2.25 a tonne firmer at $171.50, but brokers noted that volumes were thin. September Brent recovered from a low of $18.63 and at 1730 GMT was trading at $18.91 a barrel, three cents off Thursday's close.
"There's some cat crackers that have gone down and the cracks were blown out...but it's thinner than normal volumes," said one broker.

Two catalytic converters, one at the BP/Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam and one at the BP/Mobil Coryton refinery in the U.K. were shut down on Friday due to technical problems, taking out 115,000 barrels per day of capacity.
In addition, Shell confirmed on Friday that the cat cracker at its Pernis refinery will be down for an unscheduled stoppage in August followed by a scheduled stoppage of two months.
Brent made a strong recovery in late afternoon trade, tracking a similar move on NYMEX crude.
"Brent is poised to move up," said one broker. "It's tested the downside today but not really broken support."
